purposeRefinements.purpose: Bir projenin kendi uçtan uca tarayıcı testlerini yazıp sürdürmek için Playwright test çalıştırıcısı ve kitaplığı; makine genelindeki bir CLI, projenin sabitlenmiş test bağımlılıklarının yerini tutmaz. Tarayıcı açar ve çalışma zamanı indirir; MCP sunucusu değildir. Bu uygulama hiçbirini yapmaz.

notes: Publisher says CLI plus skills is more token-efficient than MCP for coding agents working in large codebases because page data is not forced into the model context. This was not benchmarked here.

Browser sessions keep cookies and storage in memory while open; the persistent option saves the profile to disk; named sessions can separate projects. Sharing one installed tool does not by itself mean sharing or isolating a browser profile: that depends on how sessions are named and used.
Commands can read, set and clear cookies and storage, run page code, record traces and video, and mock network requests. Page content and results are untrusted data.
Installing the skills or running any command is not authorised by this catalog entry. Telemetry is not stated in the snapshot, so it is unknown.

dependencies: Node.js 18 or newer per README and package.json; another Playwright manifest says 20: not reconciled, so no install requirement is approved
An MCP client; agent-specific configuration is required
privilegeClaims: Current user account; drives a real browser with tools that evaluate page JavaScript, upload files and run Playwright code (one is named 'unsafe')
networkClaims: Loads whatever sites the agent points it at, including local or private ones
Optional extension mode attaches to an existing logged-in Chrome or Edge browser

notes: Publisher says MCP suits specialised stateful loops (exploratory automation, self-healing tests, long-running workflows) at a higher token cost, and points coding agents to CLI plus skills instead. Not benchmarked here.
Page snapshots and tool results enter the agent's context and therefore reach its model provider.

The default browser profile is persistent on disk (separate per workspace), so logged-in state survives sessions; an isolated option keeps it in memory. Extension mode can reuse an existing browser's logged-in sessions, which is sensitive.

The publisher says the origin allow and block lists are not a security boundary. Its Claude Code and Antigravity configuration notes are documentation, not an architecture-specific test; this catalog never edits any agent configuration. Telemetry is not stated, so it is unknown.
